reference_notes: Structure follows the Report Tool product in tqkng/docs. Path convention follows the newer products: <slug>/<section>/...

navigation.container: docs.json navigation.products[] entry with product = {product_name} and pages = six groups
navigation.numbering: Titles carry section numbers 1.1 to 6.6. Overview and architecture file names carry the arc42 prefix 01 to 12.

pages.title: 1.1 {product_name}
pages.description: Overview of {product_name}, its purpose, source repository and the documentation sections.
sections: Opening paragraphs: what the product is, who it serves, current implementation limits
1.1.1 Product visuals (optional figures with bold figure captions)
<Info> block with repository link and source commit
1.1.2 Scope: framework used (arc42, C4) and intended audience
1.1.3 Navigation: three-column table 'I want to... | Start here | What I will find' with six rows, one per section
### Overview shortcuts: dot-separated links to the four overview pages

pages.title: 1.2 Introduction and Goals
pages.description: Understand {product_name}'s current behavior, intended goals, requirements, quality targets and stakeholders.
sections: Summary table: Main Goal, Business Domain, Size, Strategic Decision, Technologies
1.2.1 Introduction
1.2.2 Requirements: ID | Requirement | Explanation, F-prefixed IDs with sub-IDs
1.2.3 Architecture quality goals: ID (QG-n) | Priority | Quality Goal | Description, three to five goals
1.2.4 Stakeholders: Role | Responsibility | Expectation

pages.title: 1.3 Constraints
sections: 1.3.1 Technical Constraints: ID (TC) | Constraint | Explanation
1.3.2 Organizational Constraints: ID (OC) | Constraint | Explanation
1.3.3 Conventions: ID (C) | Convention | Explanation

pages.title: 1.4 Context and Scope
sections: 1.4.1 Business Context: business context diagram, then one bold-titled paragraph per user or external system
1.4.2 System Context: system context diagram
1.4.3 External interfaces: Communication partner | Input | Output | Interface or channel

pages.title: 1.5 Solution Strategy
sections: 1.5.1 Strategy summary: Solution Strategy | Quality Goal (QG-n references)

pages.title: 2.1 Building Block View
sections: 2.1.1 Level 1 - System Whitebox: whitebox diagram, then 'Container responsibilities' table (Container | Responsibility | Technology | Owned data | Inbound | Outbound)
2.1.2 Level 2 - Component view: only when justified in one sentence, one component diagram per container
2.1.3 Level 3 - Code view: optional Mermaid classDiagram

pages.title: 2.2 Runtime View
sections: 2.2.n SD-RT-nn: <scenario>, one Mermaid sequenceDiagram with autonumber per scenario
Use alt blocks for failure and recovery paths, one sentence of lead-in per scenario
pages.notes: Runtime scenarios stay in Mermaid by decision. No draw.io template.

pages.title: 2.3 Deployment View
sections: 2.3.1 Deployment view: deployment diagram of the confirmed environments only
Optional tables for runtime modes, configuration and pipelines when evidence exists

pages.title: 2.4 Crosscutting Concepts
sections: 2.4.1 Domain Entity Model: Mermaid classDiagram followed by a Term | Definition table
2.4.n further concepts (validation, errors, configuration, observability, resilience) with links to canonical security and API pages

pages.title: 2.5 Architecture Decisions
sections: Lead paragraph: what the decision set covers and where the evidence comes from
Index table: ID | Decision | Status | Decision date, IDs link to child pages
Consolidated or superseded decisions stay in the index with a short explanatory H2
Scope of this decision set: topics not yet decided, linked to Risks and Technical Debt

pages.title: AD-{number} {decision}
sections: Status line: **Status:** ... **Decision date:** ... **Implementation:** ...
Context and decision drivers
Options considered: Option | Assessment at decision time
Decision and rationale
Consequences: bullet list
Implementation evidence: permalinks at the pinned commit
Revisit when
pages.notes: One page per material decision, nested in the 'Decision records' group. Never invent options, dates or rationale.

pages.title: 2.6 Quality Requirements
sections: Pointer to the quality goals in 1.2.3
2.6.1 Verified mechanisms: Quality Goal | Quality concern | Verified implementation

pages.title: 2.7 Risks and Technical Debt
sections: 2.7.1 Risks: ID (R-nnn) | Risk | Probability | Potential impact | Priority | Mitigation
2.7.2 Technical Debt: ID (TD-nnn) | Technical debt | Affected building block in Section 2.1 | Evidence and consequence
2.7.3 Remediation order: numbered list
Evidence links after each table; never reproduce credential values

pages.title: 2.8 Glossary
sections: Lead sentence naming the pinned commit
Term | Definition table, alphabetical, terms taken only from this project

pages.title: 3. Getting started
pages.description: Set up and verify {product_name} with the documented limits of the current repository.
sections: Lead paragraph: audience and pinned commit, repository-backed steps versus work still to do
Choose your path: Path | Read in order | Outcome
Current setup limits: honest list of missing provisioning, committed secrets, absent tests

pages.title: 3.1 Prerequisites and configuration
sections: Lead paragraph with commit and safe-account advice
Choose a path (bullets)
Required settings: Setting | Used for | Where to set it
Keep settings out of the repository

pages.title: 3.2 Run locally
sections: Numbered steps taken only from repository evidence
Expected result of each step

pages.title: 3.3 Run with containers
sections: Container build and run steps from committed files

pages.title: 3.4 Verify the first result
sections: A controlled first run with an observable pass or fail result

pages.title: 3.5 Deploy
sections: Only the deployment path the repository establishes

pages.title: 3.6 Troubleshoot setup and first runs
sections: Symptom | Likely cause | Action table

pages.title: 4.1 {product_name} API
pages.description: Explore the {product_name} API contract and how it relates to what is implemented.
sections: What the API covers and whether it is implemented or proposed
Link to the OpenAPI download when a spec exists

pages.title: 4.2 Servers and authentication
sections: Placeholder statement when hosts are examples
Tabs: one tab per example or real server
Authentication: scheme, header, scoping and error codes

pages.title: 4.3 Getting started
sections: First request and response
Confirm hosts, auth and schema before drafting

pages.title: 4.4 Requests and lifecycle
sections: Request rules, limits, idempotency, pagination, states and lifecycle

pages.title: 4.5 Error responses
sections: Error envelope and code table

pages.title: 4.6 {resource}
sections: One page or generated group per resource from a reviewed OpenAPI file
Never hand-invent routes, schemas or examples

pages.title: Models
sections: Schemas from the reviewed OpenAPI file

pages.title: 5.1 Security and Privacy Overview
sections: Lead paragraph: what is handled, what the section defines
Security boundaries: Boundary | Required control
Protected information
Responsibilities
Operating principles
Read next: links to the other four pages

pages.title: 5.2 Credentials and Access Control
sections: Identity, roles, secret handling and rotation from evidence

pages.title: 5.3 Data Handling and Privacy
sections: Data classes, retention, jurisdictions only when confirmed

pages.title: 5.4 Security Risks and Required Actions
pages.description: Security Risks and Required Actions for {product_name}.
sections: Release-blocking controls: ID (SEC-nn) | Finding | Required outcome | Owner role
Control groups as H2 sections
Required verification: bullet list
Source evidence links

pages.title: 5.5 Incident Response
sections: Ownership, triage, containment, communication and review from confirmed answers

pages.title: 6.1 Release Notes
sections: Lead paragraph
Release index: Entry | Status | Date | Read more
How to use these notes
Entry format (Keep a Changelog)
Source baseline links
Last documentation review: date

pages.title: 6.2 Unreleased
sections: Added, Changed, Fixed, Security as H2 sections, empty ones omitted
Compatibility and migration
Release completion criteria

pages.title: 6.3 v{major}.{minor}.{patch}
sections: Version, date, user impact, notable changes, required actions, evidence links
pages.notes: Only for a published GitHub release or tag. A package version is not a release.

pages.title: 6.4 Repository Milestones
sections: Changes in the main branch after the last release, with commit links

pages.title: 6.5 Known Issues
sections: Issue | Impact | Workaround table

pages.title: 6.6 Upgrade and Rollback
sections: Before upgrading
Staging verification
Production promotion (numbered)
Rollback triggers and procedure
Versioning and release evidence
